newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at seven percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at seven percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money recovered slightly to seven percent after falling to six percent on Monday morning, dealers said.
They said sustained ample supply from the central bank at the year-end kept the market flushed with liquidity.
"It's quite unusual that we have no liquidity problem at all this year-end," one local bank dealer said.
He said the central bank's offer of overnight papers at seven percent helped overnight money to rebound slightly.

The central bank offered 3-4 day SBIs at seven percent, 7-8 day at 10.0 percent, 9-11 day at 10.5 percent, 14-16 day at 11.0 percent, 17-18 day at 11.25 percent, 21-25 day at 11.75 percent, one-month at 12.25 percent, three-month at 13.0 percent, six at 13.25 and 12-month at 13.50 percent.
The central bank injected 3.669 trillion rupiah into the market early on Monday. Dealers said they expected the ample condition to continue on Thursday when the market reopens.
The market will be closed on December 31 and January 1.
Dealers said local operators were squeezed on tight dollar liquidity on Monday following rises in offshore markets.
One said overnight dollar deposit rate soared to a high of 11.0 percent against the usual rate of 5.5 percent.
The dealer attributed the rise to year-end factors when banks had to square positions to close the books. One-week dollar deposit rate was at 6.375/6.50 percent.
One-month rupiah was quoted at 13.00/13.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 8.49 percent, compared with 9.46 percent on Thursday.
